Isodiv Explorer

How internally diverse is each language lineage, measured as amount of lexical change (no clock, no counting of languages), and how far apart are different lineages? Data: ASJP v21 40-item word lists.

isodiv home · How the numbers are made · Source and data

Maximum diversity per lineage

Dot: D_max, the effective number of lineages whose word lists cannot be tied together (log scale). 1 means one lineage; n mutually unrelated lects score about n. Line: how far the score moves when 10 of the 40 concepts are left out (5–95% of 30 resamples), centred on the dot; it does not include the effect of which doculects were sampled. Lineages with 2 doculects are lower bounds. Share of the unrelated maximum rescales each lineage against a set of the same size whose members are all from different families: (D_max − 1) / (D_unrelated − 1). 0 is one lineage and 1 is as diverse as unrelated lects. It removes the effect of sample size, so large and small lineages compare fairly. Widest pair is on the distance scale instead: the largest distance between two lists of the lineage, with each list replaced by its near-identical relatives so that one noisy pair cannot set it, and lists that are closer to another family than to their own left out. It uses no subgrouping. It means the most divergent pair, not the earliest split: an old list such as Hittite or Akkadian has had less time to change than two modern lists, and above about 0.95 every deep family reaches the unrelated level.

Distance between two varieties

Pick each variety by ISO 639-1 or ISO 639-3 code, Glottocode or name. The distance is computed here, in your browser, from the ASJP v21 40-item word lists, with the same PMI-LDND as the rest of this page. A code can match several word lists (several transcriptions of one language, or the members of a macrolanguage such as zh), so every pair of lists is scored and the median is reported.

What is measured

  1. Distance, not time. PMI-LDND on ASJP 40-item lists: LDND (Wichmann et al. 2010) with word distances from alignments scored by learned sound correspondences (pointwise mutual information, after Jäger 2013, 2018) instead of a flat cost per changed segment, so regular correspondences such as Japonic h : p count as close. Divided by the same measure for different meanings to remove chance resemblance. About 0 for identical lists and about 1 for unrelated languages.
  2. Diversity that ignores duplicates. Similarity Z is 1 at the median distance between two lists of the same language () and falls linearly to 0 at , the distance at which a permutation test detects a related pair half the time (scripts/regularity_eval.py). Then the Leinster–Meckes maximum diversity D_max(Z): the effective number of lineages that the word lists cannot tie together. Adding a doculect identical to one already present does not change it, and n unrelated lects score about n.
  3. No clock, no fitted scale. Both anchors are measured from the data: the same-language noise and the limit of detectable relatedness. The older similarity exp(−k·PMI-LDND) with k calibrated on same-language pairs (k_cal = ) is kept for comparison and in Scale profiles; it treated unrelated lects as about 0.64 similar, which squeezed every score under 1.57.

Reading it

  • Resolution. Beyond about two lists of 40 words cannot be told from unrelated ones, so a deep family whose branches are that far apart counts each branch as a separate lineage. D_max of a deep family is therefore partly a measure of how much of it the data can still tie together. Tests of regular sound correspondences on longer lists (NorthEuraLex, up to 1,000 concepts) do not extend this: they detect loans as readily as inheritance.
  • Same-language doculect pairs differ by PMI-LDND (10th / 50th / 90th percentile). Lineages in the lowest band cannot be ranked against each other.
  • D_max measures diversity, not relatedness. Purple rows are constructed sets, not families: random sets of lects from unrelated families, and proposed or rejected groupings such as Altaic. Unrelated lects are as diverse as it gets, so a random set scores above a real family with the same number of doculects; the deepest real families get close to the ceiling only when they have hundreds of documented doculects. A low score for a proposed grouping says its members are similar, which shared descent and long contact both produce; it is not evidence for or against the grouping. scripts/adversarial.py.
  • D_max is stable against duplicates, not against sampling more distinct varieties. Lineages with few doculects are lower bounds.
  • Contact shortens distances. The 40-item list resists borrowing but is not immune.
  • Doculects listed in config/exclusions.tsv are left out of every number here, each with its reason. scripts/audit.py flags candidates (far from the rest of the lineage, fewer than 30 of 40 concepts, or removing it lowers D_max by half a lineage or more) but never excludes automatically. A deep branch such as Chuvash is flagged and kept; a list distorted by contact or a transcription problem is excluded.
  • Widest pair. The largest single distance in a big lineage is mostly the noise tail: with thousands of pairs of 40-item lists, two ordinary lists land above the unrelated level by chance. Each list is therefore represented by itself and up to four nearest lists inside the same-language noise band, pairs are compared by the median over these neighbourhoods, and the widest such pair is reported. A list with no close relative counts in full (an old branch with one list), unless the nearest list of another family is closer than the nearest of its own: that flags contact or a mixed or mislabelled list (Aynu, Mogogodo). Only lineage membership is used, no internal classification. scripts/widest.py.
  • Depth. Distances are mapped to retention, the share of basic vocabulary still cognate (100% = as close as two lists of one language), on a curve fitted to expert cognate coding in ten Lexibank datasets (each dataset's coding strictness taken out as a constant). A lineage's depth is 100% minus the retention across its deepest split, i.e. the share of basic vocabulary no longer shared there: average-linkage clustering on τ = −ln retention, the median across the root split. A lineage's own ancestors (Latin for Romance, Old Chinese for Sinitic) are left out, since an ancestor is not a branch. Above about 79% the 40 words cannot resolve depth: those lineages are shown as beyond the horizon. Depth measures change, not time. scripts/depth.py.
  • Doculects: every ASJP doculect of a lineage is used (up to 2,000 for Atlantic-Congo), after dropping those with too little overlap with the others. A lineage that contains others (Oceanic inside Austronesian) therefore contains all of their doculects, and since D_max cannot fall when doculects are added, a family never scores below one of its subfamilies. Earlier versions capped each lineage at 80 doculects separately, and Oceanic could outscore Austronesian. The concept resampling uses at most 40 doculects, so its range is shown as a width around the estimate, and between-lineage comparisons use 25.
  • Size. Related lects are closer than unrelated ones, so a real family scores below an unrelated assortment of the same size; across sizes, a large deep family can still outscore a few unrelated lects, because it holds more lineages the data cannot tie together. The share-of-unrelated-maximum view divides by an unrelated assortment's score at the lineage's own number of doculects (measured up to 80 lects, extended beyond that with n / (1 + (n − 1)·z̄)).

Wichmann, Holman, Bakker & Brown 2010, Physica A 389. Leinster & Meckes 2016, Entropy 18(3). ASJP Database v21, CC-BY-4.0.
